note: A jam in three aims: {{6}} of Dorian over the 4th chord on a solo-over, {{b7}} of Mixolydian over the ♭7th chord, then one long Dorian solo across three framed positions. The chords are tokens counted the long way once, the key is moves (any key) and named only as {{=key}}, the last block now has the positions on a position-neck, and it ends with the variation that makes the solo the learner's own.

exercise.title: The jam
exercise.why: A phrase can aim at the 6th, the ♭7 or a root after a crossing, so a solo is choosing which one each phrase goes for.

cells.text:
The backing track loops two chords of {{=key}} Dorian. {{chord:i7}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV7}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track. Improvise in {{=key}} Dorian, in any position you like, and land on {{6}} each time {{chord:IV7}} comes round.
Practice until your fingers find {{6}} before the chord changes.

Press Play below to start the backing track in {{=key}} Mixolydian: {{chord:I}}, then {{chord:bVII}}, the chord built on {{b7}}, then {{chord:IV}} and {{chord:I}} again. Under it are positions 1 and 2 of the {{=key}} Mixolydian scale, with {{1}} and {{b7}} ringed.
Improvise in the two positions, and hold a ringed {{b7}} through the {{chord:bVII}} bar.
If the bar passes before you find {{b7}}, play only the ringed notes for a few rounds.

Press Play below to start the backing track on {{chord:i7}} and {{chord:IV7}} again. Under it are positions 1, 2 and 3 of the {{=key}} Dorian scale. Play one long solo that climbs from position 1 to position 3 and comes back down, and choose what each phrase aims for: {{6}}, a ringed {{1}} or the slide into the next position.
Keep the one phrase you like best, and start your next solo from it.
{{?key}}In another key the positions sit on other frets, and {{6}} is still the 3rd of {{chord:IV7}}.
